Based on the healthcare Q&A matches provided, it appears that the standard treatment approach for locally advanced squamous cell carcinoma (SCC) of the esophagus does not typically involve a combination of chemoradiotherapy and surgery. The study suggests that there is no difference in clinical toxicity profiles or survival outcomes with either definitive chemoradiotherapy or chemoradiation followed by surgery.

In fact, the matches indicate that surgical resection may not be necessary for patients with locally advanced esophageal cancer, as the overall objective of treatment remains the same - to achieve a complete response and control of the disease. The study suggests that preoperative platelet count is a predictive factor for long-term survival in ESCC patients, implying that it may also be relevant when considering the management of this particular type of cancer.

However, it's essential to note that individual patient situations can vary greatly, and the decision to proceed with surgery or not should always be made on an ad hoc basis, taking into account factors such as overall health, tumor size, location, and personal preferences. It is also crucial to discuss these questions and any treatment decisions with a qualified healthcare professional.

In summary, based on the provided information, it seems that chemoradiotherapy followed by surgery may not be the standard of care for locally advanced squamous cell carcinoma of the esophagus, but preoperative platelet count is a relevant factor in predicting survival outcomes.
